did: I worked through the open dependency updates. Two went in once their checks passed: seroval, which came in while I worked, and the vite group. The other three are checked and reviewed, and are with the coordinator, who now does the merging. They are the TypeScript lint tooling (it replaced the tsc-alias update), react-separator and wasm-bindgen-test. A second agent read each one with fresh eyes, since Codex was out of reviews, and found nothing that blocks. I also found that a dependabot command posted from my tools arrives with dots inserted, so dependabot never sees it, and that main only takes a pull request that is up to date with it.
left: I didn't merge the TypeScript lint tooling, react-separator or wasm-bindgen-test myself. Partway through, the coordinator took over all merging, so each waits on its branch being brought up to date and its checks passing once more.
The wasm-bindgen-test update has only been checked against main as it stood on Nov 5. Bringing it up to date is the first time it runs against today's code.
I left the WASM release, the flake update and every pull request a person opened alone, as I was asked.
